item: Clause-count-free restriction lemma (Lemma 2.1, 'Restriction bound'): under a p-random restriction, a width-k CNF H satisfies |E G·H_{T,rho}| <= W(H,T,rho)·corr_b(G) for every G, with E W <= 1/(1-theta), theta = sum_{l>b} C(k,l)(2p/(1-p))^l, valid for any constant pk (b chosen large) and independent of the number of clauses
item_type: F3 (lemma; F5 flavour: change of representation of a restricted CNF into a signed mixture of narrow CNFs)
method_note: Text-level only. The Lean was NOT compiled (no local toolchain, no local Mathlib checkout). Chain traced by reading proofs; grep over OAI/Computability for reuse. The web precedent searches, rate-limited in the first pass, were rerun on 2026-10-10 (38 WebSearch queries, none rate-limited, plus GitHub repository search). WebFetch could reach github.com but failed with DNS errors (ENOTFOUND) for arxiv.org, export.arxiv.org, alphaxiv.org, eccc.weizmann.ac.il, lacker.io and mathweb.ucsd.edu, so several literature claims rest on search-result abstracts and snippets, not on full texts; see precedent_check.update_2026_10_10_web.
lean_status_why: cnf_restriction_bound (Restriction.lean:59) states Lemma 2.1 exactly: W depends only on H and the restriction, restrictionAvg p W <= 1/(1-theta) with the paper's theta, and |E G·H_restricted| <= W·corr b G for all real G. The proof follows the paper's route (violation-path expansion, marker mixture, reweighting, backward counting) in Restriction*/MarkerMixture/ReversePath* files, and the comparator target consumes it through wide_correlation_of_good_restrictions.
lean_gaps: No mathematical gap found. The comparator uses only the theta <= 1/2 corollary (restrictionAvg_cnfRestrictionCost_le_two, bound 2); the general 1/(1-theta) form is also proved (restrictionAvg_cnfRestrictionCost_le).

W is the explicit cnfRestrictionCost: a sum over violation paths, up to card V/(b+1) layers, of products of reciprocal covered-clause counts. It is computed on H.normalize, which drops tautological and true clauses as the paper does.
corr b G is a sup over narrowTests b, i.e. all Boolean functions on the live cube computable by some width-<=b CNF. This matches corr_b.
Restriction law: each coordinate is live with probability p, else fixed to each bit with probability (1-p)/2. Matches the paper.

The downstream counting lemma circuit_lower_bound_of_small_cnf_correlations is generic in f but hard-wires the omega(sqrt n) constants (k >= 3(s+1)sqrt d, correlation <= 6·2^{-4(s+1)sqrt d}). Reusing it for parity-type c·sqrt(n) bounds needs a re-parametrised copy.

Load-bearing: the restriction cluster (Restriction*.lean, ReversePath*.lean, Marker*.lean) is 4,238 of 25,007 lines; Tape*/Machine*/Language* plumbing is 12,740 lines. The novelty pass gives a DAG closure of 16.9% overall and about 38% of the lower-bound sub-DAG.

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.Circuit3
lean_source.text:
structure Circuit3 (V : Type uV) where
  bottomCount : ℕ
  middleCount : ℕ
  bottom : Fin bottomCount → RawClause V
  middle : Fin middleCount → Finset (Fin bottomCount)
  top : Finset (Fin middleCount)

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.Restriction / Live
lean_source.text:
abbrev Restriction (V : Type uDepth1) := V → Option Bool
abbrev Live {V : Type uDepth2} (σ : Restriction V) := {v : V // σ v = none}

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.restrictionAvg
lean_source.text:
def restrictionCoordinateWeight (p : ℝ) : Option Bool → ℝ
  | none => p
  | some _ => (1 - p) / 2

def restrictionWeight {V : Type uDepth11} [Fintype V] (p : ℝ) (σ : Restriction V) : ℝ :=
  ∏ v, restrictionCoordinateWeight p (σ v)

def restrictionAvg {V : Type uDepth12} [Fintype V] (p : ℝ)
    (F : Restriction V → ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ σ, restrictionWeight p σ * F σ

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.corr
OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.pathWeight / pathCost / restrictionCost
OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.restrictionTheta
lean_source.text:
def restrictionTheta (k b : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : ℝ :=
  ∑ l ∈ Finset.Icc (b + 1) k, (k.choose l : ℝ) * (2 * p / (1 - p)) ^ l

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.cnfRestrictionCost
lean_source.text:
def cnfRestrictionCost (H : CNF V) (b : ℕ) (σ : Restriction V) : ℝ :=
  restrictionCost (cnfIndexFamily H.normalize) b σ

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.cnf_restricted_correlation_le_cost
lean_source.text:
theorem cnf_restricted_correlation_le_cost (H : CNF V) (b : ℕ) (hb : 1 ≤ b)
    (σ : Restriction V) (G : Cube (Live σ) → ℝ) :
    |finiteAvg (fun x => G x * indicator (H.eval (fill σ x)))| ≤
      cnfRestrictionCost H b σ * corr b G :=

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.cnf_restriction_bound
lean_source.text:
theorem cnf_restriction_bound (H : CNF V) (b k : ℕ) (hb : 1 ≤ b)
    (hH : H.WidthAtMost k) (p : ℝ) (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1)
    (hθ : restrictionTheta k b p < 1) :
    ∃ W : Restriction V → ℝ,
      (∀ σ, 0 ≤ W σ) ∧
      restrictionAvg p W ≤ 1 / (1 - restrictionTheta k b p) ∧
      ∀ (σ : Restriction V) (G : Cube (Live σ) → ℝ),
        |finiteAvg (fun x => G x * indicator (H.eval (fill σ x)))| ≤ W σ * corr b G :=

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.restrictionAvg_cnfRestrictionCost_le_two
lean_source.text:
theorem restrictionAvg_cnfRestrictionCost_le_two (H : CNF V) (b k : ℕ)
    (hH : H.WidthAtMost k) (p : ℝ) (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1)
    (hθ : restrictionTheta k b p ≤ 1 / 2) :
    restrictionAvg p (cnfRestrictionCost H b) ≤ 2 :=

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.indexedCNF_restriction_expansion
lean_source.text:
theorem indexedCNF_restriction_expansion (C : I → Clause V) (b : ℕ)
    (σ : Restriction V) (x : Cube (Live σ)) :
    indicator ((indexedCNF C).eval (fill σ x)) =
      indicator ((easyBaseCNF C b σ).eval x) +
        ∑ j ∈ Finset.range ((liveSet σ).card / (b + 1)),
          (-1 : ℝ) ^ (j + 1) * pathLayer C b σ (easyBaseCNF C b σ) (j + 1) x :=

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.restrictionAvg_restrictionCost_le
lean_source.text:
theorem restrictionAvg_restrictionCost_le (C : I → Clause V) (p : ℝ)
    (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (b k : ℕ)
    (hn : ∀ i, (C i).Normalized) (hwidth : ∀ i, (C i).scope.card ≤ k)
    (hθ : reverseTheta (2 * p / (1 - p)) b k < 1) :
    restrictionAvg p (fun σ => restrictionCost C b σ) ≤
      (1 - reverseTheta (2 * p / (1 - p)) b k)⁻¹ :=

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.wide_correlation_of_good_restrictions
lean_source.text:
theorem wide_correlation_of_good_restrictions {p ε : ℝ}
    (hp0 : 0 < p) (hp1 : p < 1) (hε : 0 ≤ ε)
    (b k : ℕ) (hb : 1 ≤ b) (hθ : restrictionTheta k b p ≤ 1 / 2)
    (f : Cube V → Bool)
    (hbad : restrictionAvg p (fun σ => if ¬ goodRestriction p ε b f σ then 1 else 0) ≤
      4 * ε) :
    ∀ H : CNF V, H.WidthAtMost k →
      |finiteAvg (fun x => sign (f x) * indicator (H.eval x))| ≤ 6 * ε :=

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.circuit_lower_bound_of_small_cnf_correlations
lean_source.text:
theorem circuit_lower_bound_of_small_cnf_correlations
    (d k : ℕ) (s : ℝ) (hs : 0 ≤ s) (hd : 4 ≤ d)
    (hk : 3 * (s + 1) * Real.sqrt (d : ℝ) ≤ (k : ℝ))
    (f : Cube (Fin d) → Bool)
    (hcorr : ∀ H : CNF (Fin d), H.WidthAtMost k →
      |finiteAvg (fun x : Cube (Fin d) => sign (f x) * indicator (H.eval x))| ≤
        6 * (2 : ℝ) ^ (-(64 * (s + 1) * Real.sqrt (d : ℝ)) / 16))
    (C : Circuit3 (Fin d)) (hC : C.Computes f) :
    (2 : ℝ) ^ (s * Real.sqrt (d : ℝ)) < (C.gateCount : ℝ) :=

lean_source.name: OAI.DepthThreeLowerBound.exists_polynomial_time_language_depth_three_lower_bound
lean_source.text:
theorem exists_polynomial_time_language_depth_three_lower_bound :
    ∃ (L : List Bool → Bool) (M : FiniteMultiTapeMachine) (C a : ℕ),
      0 < C ∧ 0 < a ∧
      (∀ w : List Bool, MultiTapeHaltsIn M w (L w) (C * (w.length + 1) ^ a)) ∧
      ∀ A : ℝ, 0 < A → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n →
        ∀ D : Circuit3 (Fin n), D.Computes (fun x => L (List.ofFn x)) →
          (2 : ℝ) ^ (A * Real.sqrt (n : ℝ)) < (D.gateCount : ℝ) :=

speedup_targets.title: Depth-3 parity lower bound 2^{Omega(sqrt n)} (Håstad 1986/89; PPZ99 sharp form)
speedup_targets.statement: Every OR-AND-OR circuit computing parity of n bits has 2^{c·sqrt n} gates for some absolute c > 0 (sharp: Theta(n^{1/4} 2^{sqrt n}), PPZ99).
speedup_targets.reference: J. Håstad, 'Almost optimal lower bounds for small depth circuits', STOC 1986 / Computational limitations of small-depth circuits (MIT Press 1987), cited as H89; Paturi-Pudlák-Zane, 'Satisfiability coding lemma', Chicago J. TCS 1999, Thm 6; HJP95 Thm 3.3.
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: Switching-lemma route: about 8-10 pages including the switching lemma. PPZ route: about 3-4 pages. No Lean formalization known (see switching_lemma_formalizations).
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: With C1 and the f-generic Lean skeleton (wide_correlation_of_good_restrictions plus a re-parametrised circuit_lower_bound_of_small_cnf_correlations), the only new ingredient is a parity-vs-narrow-CNF correlation bound corr_b(parity on m live vars) <= 2^{-Omega(m/b)}. That bound is expected true but was NOT verified here, and the paper does not state it. Taking b = O(1) and pk a small constant gives 2^{c sqrt n}. This replaces the switching lemma by C1. It would not beat the short PPZ argument, so the gain is mainly against the switching-lemma route.
speedup_targets.expected_speedup: medium vs switching-lemma route; low vs PPZ

speedup_targets.title: Bounded independence fools CNFs (Bazzi 2009; Razborov's simplified proof)
speedup_targets.statement: Every polylog(m/epsilon)-wise independent distribution epsilon-fools every m-clause CNF.
speedup_targets.reference: L. Bazzi, 'Polylogarithmic independence can fool DNF formulas', SICOMP 38 (2009); A. Razborov, 'A simple proof of Bazzi's theorem', ACM TOCT 1 (2009).
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: Razborov: about 5 pages; no formalization known.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: Speculative. C1 says a randomly restricted wide CNF is, in the dual (correlation) sense, an O(1)-mass mixture of width-b CNFs, with no dependence on the number of clauses. If width-b CNFs are fooled by O(b)-wise-independent restrictions, a clause-count-free fooling statement could follow. But Bazzi's bound depends on m only polylogarithmically, and fooling needs the distribution itself, not a random restriction, so the fit is weak.

switching_lemma_formalizations: UPDATED 2026-10-10 (web): switching-lemma formalizations DO exist, all outside Mathlib and outside the release. (1) arXiv 2609.24188 'Formalizing PARITY Circuit Lower Bounds in Lean' (Sept 2026). The full text was not fetchable. Search snippets say it states Hastad's switching lemma (O'Donnell's presentation) as a ratio of bad restrictions to all restrictions using Mathlib countP, with constant 10 under an extra rounding hypothesis (40 without), and discusses Razborov's encoding (d lg w + 2d auxiliary bits). Whether it includes a depth-3 parity bound is unknown. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.24188 (2) github.com/codula-code/SwitchingLemma, created 2026-09-03: per its README, a standalone Lean 4 proof in core Lean (no Mathlib), toolchain v4.33.1, of Hastad 2014 SIAM Lemma 3.3 via reweighting Lemma 3.4. The bound is Pr[DT depth >= h] <= (10 w eps)^h for width-w DNFs, plus a conditional version. The README claims no sorry and only the standard axioms (unverified here). https://github.com/codula-code/SwitchingLemma (3) github.com/Quantyra/formal-switching-lemma (v0.10.0, Lean v4.13.0), cited in 2609.24188 as Fredriksen's work: a SimpleDNF switching lemma (switchingLemmaTermSimple_proved) with CNF duals and layer schedules. Its README disclaims a general PHP switching lemma. https://github.com/Quantyra/formal-switching-lemma No Isabelle AFP or Coq switching-lemma entry was found; bounded-arithmetic formalizations (APC1, Krajicek PV1+WPHP) exist but are not proof-assistant code. Mathlib d13f23b still has no circuit-complexity library (no local checkout to grep). Consequence for targets: the 'formal proof to compare: none in Lean' notes in the depth-3 parity and depth-hierarchy targets are now stale. Comparator candidates exist, on different toolchains (v4.13.0, v4.33.1) from the pinned v4.34.1 and possibly without Mathlib. The earlier local greps still hold: the release's lean/OAI never mentions switching or Hastad, and DepthThree deliberately avoids the switching lemma.

open_problems.title: An explicit function with depth-3 complexity 2^{n^{1/2+epsilon}} (HJP95 Problem 2)
open_problems.statement: Find an explicit f with S_3(f) >= 2^{n^{1/2+epsilon}} for a fixed epsilon > 0.
open_problems.reference: Håstad-Jukna-Pudlák, 'Top-down lower bounds for depth-three circuits', Comput. Complexity 5 (1995), Sec. 5 Problem 2; GPPST24 Sec. 1.1; GKPRT26 (arXiv 2601.04446).
open_problems.obstruction_match: Exact match of the barrier C1 partly breaks. C1 needs pk = O(1) for a constant b. At width k ~ n^{1/2+epsilon} this forces p ~ n^{-1/2-epsilon}, so the live set m ~ n^{1/2-epsilon} is smaller than k and the slice correlation 2^{-m/16} cannot beat 2^{-k}. Letting pk grow forces b to grow, and the sparse partition then becomes tower-sized.
open_problems.adaptation_sketch: Either a version of C1 with E W <= 2 for pk = n^{delta} at b = n^{O(delta)}, or slices whose corr_b decays like 2^{-m·g(b)} with g growing.

negative_controls.title: N1 (proved-false analogue): parity requires 2^{omega(sqrt n)} depth-3 gates
negative_controls.statement: False: parity has OR-AND-OR circuits of size O(n^{1/4} 2^{sqrt n}) (PPZ99).
negative_controls.why: corr_b(parity on m live vars) decays like 2^{-m/b}, at a rate that depends on b. So taking b large to allow constant pk destroys the slice bound. The C1 route must stall at c·sqrt n for parity, and a prover using C1 must not 'prove' the false statement.

top5.argument: This is the cleanest measurable device-reuse test. The statement uses only DepthThree's own Circuit3 vocabulary, the downstream skeleton (wide_correlation_of_good_restrictions) is already generic in f, and the target is a classic switching-lemma consequence. With C1 the remaining work is a parity/narrow-CNF correlation lemma plus re-parametrised counting; without it a prover must find a switching lemma or the PPZ coding lemma. The expected gain is medium against the switching route and low against PPZ, and either outcome is informative.

This is genuine reuse of C1 on new functions. C1 reduces the open question to a pseudorandomness property of random restrictions, and the Lean pipeline after the slice is f-generic. A success would be new mathematics using the device unchanged.

C1 already controls each middle CNF's correlation; only the counting step uses exact computation. A prover with C1 in its library should reach this much faster than one without, which makes it a good speedup probe with a plausible positive outcome.
C1 is effective, so this tests whether provers can isolate the true bottleneck (sparsification) once the device is given. Moderate payoff and moderate difficulty.
This is the true frontier. C1 provably does not suffice as stated (see obstruction_match), so it doubles as a check on whether provers over-claim. Low confidence.

precedent_check.post_release_uses: None found (web rerun 2026-10-10). Searches for the exact title, '2^{omega(sqrt n)} depth-3 2026', 'restriction lemma clause count depth-three', 'signed combination width-b CNF random restriction', OpenAI + depth-three, and the Computational Complexity blog, ECCC, Goedel's Lost Letter, Aaronson and Kalai returned no paper, preprint or blog post (after 2026-10-06) that cites, uses or discusses the restriction lemma or the 2^{omega(sqrt n)} depth-3 claim. Press coverage of the Oct 6 release (Scientific American, Gizmodo, yourstory, interestingengineering, aiweekly) surfaced, none mentioning depth-3 circuits. Index lag four days after release is a real limitation; recheck later.
precedent_check.earlier_equivalent: None found in the novelty pass. Neighbours: H89 switching (needs pk < 1/5), Razborov encoding (pays log w bits), SBI/Razborov small-p, Lovett-Wu-Zhang 2020 mild restrictions (term compression, not CNF-to-CNF correlation transfer), IMP12, GMR sparsification. No new precedent found here; the release contains no other use.
precedent_check.verdict: No downgrade. The 2026-10-10 web rerun found no earlier equivalent and no post-release use. The closest neighbours are Lovett-Wu-Zhang 2020 and SBI 2002/04. Both are mild-restriction lemmas: LWZ gives a clause-count-free first moment, and SBI was mislabelled 'small p' earlier. Neither is a correlation-preserving, clause-count-free reduction of width-k CNFs to signed mixtures of width-b CNFs at arbitrary constant pk. The 2^{omega(sqrt n)} depth-3 barrier was listed as open through 2026-08 (lacker.io) and April 2026 (Talebanfard). C1 stays N3 provisional. The residual risk is still expert folklore, plus full texts (SBI, Razborov's improvement) that could not be fetched.

barrier_open_2025_2026: Confirmed open before the release. The lacker.io problem page (search snippet says 'verified 2026-08-10') lists the 2^{omega(sqrt n)} explicit depth-3 bound as open, with record 2^{1.282 sqrt n} (PPSZ05) and parity Theta(n^{1/4} 2^{sqrt n}): https://lacker.io/complexity/problems/depth3-circuits-past-sqrt-n.html

Talebanfard, 'Depth-Three Circuits: Recent Constructions and Lower Bounds, and the Road Ahead', Sapienza DIAG, 17 April 2026; abstract: state-of-the-art lower bounds 'have not changed since the 80s': https://www.diag.uniroma1.it/node/30665

GKPRT26 'Optimal Depth-Three Circuits for Inner Product' (arXiv 2601.04446, Jan 2026) and 'Optimal Monotone Depth-Three Circuit Lower Bounds for Majority' (arXiv 2601.04072, Jan 2026) are 2026 depth-3 papers; neither claims a 2^{omega(sqrt n)} bound (abstracts via search): https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04446 , https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.04072

Open-problem statement 'wide open to prove a lower bound 2^{omega(sqrt n)} of a depth-3 circuit (or formula) computing some explicit function (e.g., a function in P, or even E^NP)': arXiv 1705.03588 (2017), https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.03588

HJP95 (Computational Complexity 5, 1995, 99-112) poses the explicit 2^{omega(sqrt n)} question, specifically for MAJ: https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/BF01268140 ; Paturi-Saks-Zane STOC 1997 says known techniques seem incapable of 2^{h(n) sqrt n} with h unbounded: https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~paturi/myPapers/pubs/PaturiSaksZane_1997_stoc.pdf

GPPST24 (CCC 2024, arXiv 2403.09134) 'Local Enumeration and Majority Lower Bounds': Sigma_3^3 Majority bound 1.251^n; optimal local-enumeration bounds would give the unrestricted 2^{omega(sqrt n)} bound: https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.CCC.2024.17

Goldreich-Wigderson (multilinear functions, depth-3) and Golovnev-Kulikov-Williams 'Circuit Depth Reductions' (ITCS 2021) frame depth-3 bounds as routes to general lower bounds via Valiant's reduction; neither breaks sqrt n: https://www.wisdom.weizmann.ac.il/~oded/p_kk.html , https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.04828
earlier_equivalents_checked: Hastad switching lemma: standard statement Pr[DT depth of F|rho >= d] <= (10 sigma w)^d for sigma <= 1/5 (Katz lecture notes), i.e. non-trivial only for pk below an absolute constant. Verified in shape; conclusion is decision-tree depth, not a clause-count-free correlation transfer at arbitrary constant pk. https://www.cs.umd.edu/~jkatz/complexity/f05/switching-lemma.pdf

Razborov encoding proof: injective map from bad restrictions to restrictions plus auxiliary bits; the Lean PARITY paper (arXiv 2609.24188) states the auxiliary bits number d lg w + 2d. Verified 'pays log w bits per step'; not equivalent. https://arxiv.org/pdf/1504.03398 , https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.24188

Rossman 2017 entropy proof: Pr[DTdepth(F|R_p) >= t] <= O(p log(m+1))^t for m-clause DNF/CNF. Verified: clause count enters as log m and p must be small; not equivalent. https://www.math.utoronto.ca/rossman/logsize.pdf

CORRECTION, Segerlind-Buss-Impagliazzo (FOCS 2002 / SICOMP 2004): the existing note lists SBI under 'small p'. That is wrong if p is the probability a variable stays free. SBI's lemma is for SMALL RESTRICTIONS, which fix only a small fraction of the variables, i.e. most variables stay free. Its hypothesis is DNFs with very small conjunctions. Its conclusion is weaker: ORs of very small ANDs become ANDs of modestly small ORs, or small-depth decision trees for small enough k. A follow-up says the restriction fixes 'a polynomially small fraction' of the bits. This makes SBI, with Razborov's improvement, a closer neighbour than recorded: a mild-restriction width-type conclusion. It is still not equivalent: it is a pointwise switching statement that needs k tiny relative to the restriction, not a signed narrow-CNF expansion with E W <= 1/(1-theta) at every constant pk. Whether its failure bound is free of the term count was NOT verified, because the full text could not be fetched. https://sites.math.rutgers.edu/~saks/DMSEM/F02/0910.html , https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~sbuss/ResearchWeb/resK/focs02.pdf , https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.02275

Lovett-Wu-Zhang, 'Decision list compression by mild random restrictions' (arXiv 1909.10658, STOC 2020): restriction lemma fixing only a small fraction of variables; E[#useful terms] <= (4/(1-alpha))^w (arXiv) / (4/alpha)^w (ECCC notation). Verified: clause-count-free first-moment bound at mild restriction rates, the closest in spirit, but its conclusion is DNF term compression (resolves GMR sparsification conjecture), not a correlation-preserving reduction of a width-k CNF to width-b CNFs. Not equivalent. https://arxiv.org/abs/1909.10658 , https://eccc.weizmann.ac.il/report/2019/137

Impagliazzo-Matthews-Paturi SODA 2012 (arXiv 1107.3127): extended switching lemma for several k-CNFs/k-DNFs simultaneously, building a restriction partition; Hastad-regime parameters. Verified; not equivalent. https://cseweb.ucsd.edu/~paturi/myPapers/pubs/ImpagliazzoMatthewsPaturi_2012_soda.pdf

Paturi-Pudlak-Zane FOCS 1997 satisfiability coding lemma: Omega(n^{1/4} 2^{sqrt n}) tight depth-3 parity bound via isolated solutions; PPSZ05 2^{1.282 sqrt n}. Verified; different mechanism, capped at sqrt n. https://courses.cs.washington.edu/courses/cse599i/24sp/papers/PaturiPudlakZane_1997_focs.pdf
Hastad-Jukna-Pudlak 1995 top-down method: 2^{0.618 sqrt n} parity, 2^{0.849 sqrt n} majority. Verified; not equivalent. https://www.csc.kth.se/~johanh/topdowndepth3.pdf

Golovnev-Kulikov-Williams 'Circuit Depth Reductions' (ITCS 2021): every size-s circuit is an OR of 2^{s/3.9} 16-CNFs; a depth-reduction result, not a restriction lemma. https://arxiv.org/abs/1811.04828

Kurur et al.: no depth-3 Boolean random-restriction paper by Kurur was found; the reference could not be identified (search 'Kurur depth-3 Boolean circuits lower bound random restriction' returned nothing by that author).

Related but not equivalent: Hastad-Rossman-Servedio-Tan average-case depth hierarchy (arXiv 1504.03398) bounds correlation of restricted Sipser functions with bounded-width CNFs via random projections, in the switching regime. Chen-Fatehpuria-Patel-Servedio 'Learning Depth-3 Circuits with Polynomial Savings' (arXiv 2609.18166, Sept 2026, before the release) improves approximate degree of width-k CNFs with a random-restriction-style argument. 'The Switching Lemma shows what the Switching Lemma cannot prove' (arXiv 2606.12631, June 2026) gives a natural-proofs-style barrier for switching-lemma properties at fixed depth; not a clause-count-free lemma. Abstracts only.

Targeted searches for a signed or alternating expansion of a restricted CNF into narrow CNFs, or for a clause-count-free width/correlation reduction at constant restriction rate, returned nothing equivalent.
corrections_to_existing_claims: SBI is a small-restriction regime (few variables fixed), not 'small p'; see above. Novelty.md's 'These work only for small p' for SBI/Razborov should be read as 'small fraction fixed, with tiny term size'.

H89 threshold: the textbook form needs sigma <= 1/5 and gives (10 sigma w)^d, so it is useful only for pk < 1/10 in that normalisation. 'Needs pk < 1/5' is roughly right as 'pk below an absolute constant'.
Release size: press reports say 722 manuscripts / 372 families (CLAUDE.md says 719); not relevant to the verdict.
